questions.prompt: In OH's 9th District House race, outside money favors Republicans by $4.7M. Whose nominee has raised more?

questions.prompt: After NRSC v. FEC (June 2026), how much can a party spend in coordination with its Senate nominee?
options: Up to a set limit per state
questions.why: The Supreme Court struck down the limits on party coordinated spending, so parties can now spend without limit alongside their candidates.

questions.prompt: Does a 501(c)(4) nonprofit that runs election ads have to disclose its donors?
questions.why: It must report the ad spending, but generally not its donors unless they gave for that ad. That's why it's called dark money.

questions.prompt: Can a super PAC give $10,000 directly to a House candidate's campaign?
questions.why: Super PACs can raise unlimited money but can't give to candidates or coordinate with them. They can only spend independently.

questions.prompt: NO GOING BACK PAC INC. (a super PAC) has spent $305K in NJ's 9th District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Republican or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.
